title: The real numbers
goal: Know that the real numbers are all points on the line, and that the rules of Chapter 1 apply to them.
generalHint: Remember: the real numbers obey the same rules as before. Use (a + b)(a − b) = a² − b².

screens.label: RECALL
screens.title: Is √2 a fraction?
screens.prompt: Look back at lesson 1.7. Is $\sqrt{2}$ a rational number?

options.label: Yes, it is rational
options.reply: Lesson 1.7 shows that no fraction has a square equal to 2. Can √2 be a fraction?

feedback.correctWhy: Lesson 1.7 proves that no fraction has a square equal to 2.

screens.caption: Choose an answer, then check.

screens.label: PUZZLE
screens.title: Is each point a fraction?
screens.prompt: Pick any point of the number line. Guess: is each point a fraction?

options.label: Yes, each point is a fraction
options.reply: The point √2 is on the line. Lesson 1.7 shows that it is not a fraction. Is each point a fraction?

options.label: No, some points are not fractions

feedback.correctTitle: No, some points are not fractions.
feedback.correctWhy: The point $\sqrt{2}$ is on the line, but it is not a fraction. You see it on the next screen.

hints: Think of $\sqrt{2}$. Where is it on the line?
screens.caption: Choose an answer, then check.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: Find √2 digit by digit
screens.prompt: Each point has a decimal. Find the decimal of $\sqrt{2}$. Pick the next digit each time. The line zooms by 10.

options.label: Yes, after some digits
options.reply: A decimal that stops is a fraction. For example, 1.414 = 1414/1000. Is √2 a fraction?

feedback.correctWhy: A decimal that stops is a fraction. The number $\sqrt{2}$ is not a fraction.

screens.caption: Pick digits until the search ends. Then answer the question.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: Real numbers
screens.prompt: Each point of the line is a real number. Real numbers have decimals, and some decimals never stop, for example 9.123145… Addition and multiplication obey the same rules as before. Each real number $a \ne 0$ has an inverse.

note.label: WORDS MATTER
note.text: Real number means a point of the line. Rational means a fraction.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: The E/I system
screens.prompt: Two objects E (even) and I (odd). Fill the two tables. Tap a cell to choose E or I. These two objects obey the same rules as numbers.

feedback.correctWhy: E acts like 0 and I acts like 1. Only these two objects obey the same rules.

interaction.wrongReply: Check each cell with real numbers. For example, 3 + 5 = 8 is I + I. Is 8 even or odd?

hints: Use numbers: 2 is even and 3 is odd. Find 2 + 3 and 2 · 3.
screens.caption: Fill all eight cells, then check.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 1 OF 1
screens.title: Use (a + b)(a − b)
screens.prompt: Find the value. Use $(a+b)(a-b) = a^2 - b^2$.

mistakes.reply: Use the formula a² − b². What is (√2)² − 1²?

screens.label: LESSON 3.1 COMPLETE
screens.title: The same rules hold.

trap.question: True or false: the rules N1–N12 apply to integers only.

options.label: True
options.reply: You used the formula a² − b² with √2. Is √2 an integer?

feedback.correctWhy: The rules hold for rational numbers and for real numbers. For example, $(\sqrt{2}+1)(\sqrt{2}-1) = 1$ uses the rules.

screens.caption: Saved to your rule book.
